drew: quick flag  bringing onboard 'tanager-compact-int8' via PTQ. seeing odd split: clustering (silhouette) tanked but recall@10 only drops for tiny queries (<5 tokens). anyone seen norm compression like this?
sam: sounds familiar. short queries hit fewer tokens so directional magnitude matters more. do you have the eval breakdown?
drew: small-scan (2.2k queries). fp recall@10=0.80, int8 recall@10=0.66 overall. short (<=5) fp=0.83 -> int8=0.49. mid (6-30) fp=0.79 -> int8=0.76. silhouette fp=0.44 -> int8=0.25.
talia: what was the quant recipe? per-tensor or per-channel? calib batch size?
drew: ONNX PTQ, per-tensor symmetric, calibration using eval batch=64, calib_samples=1024 from the eval corpus. no clamp tuning.
sam: per-tensor + large calib batch can under-estimate rare activations and compress norms. check L2 norm hist by bucket and top-dim activation ranges.
drew: pasted perf-bot summary below.
perf-bot: run summary for 3789999999:
```
model: tanager-compact-int8 (onnx ptq)
dataset: small-scan (2.2k)
metrics:
  recall@1: fp=0.58 -> int8=0.41
  recall@10: fp=0.80 -> int8=0.66
  recall@10 (<=5): fp=0.83 -> int8=0.49
  recall@10 (6-30): fp=0.79 -> int8=0.76
  silhouette: fp=0.44 -> int8=0.25
  avg-l2: fp=1.15 -> int8=0.76
notes: strong norm compression on short queries; per-tensor scales likely underflow rare-dim directions.
```
talia: try per-channel quant + reduce calib batch to 8-16 and include targeted short-query samples in calibration. also run kmeans k-sensitivity (k=30..120) and pairwise recall stability.
drew: quick ablation: switched to per-channel, calib_samples=256, calib_batch=12. short recall@10 rose 0.49 -> 0.67, silhouette 0.25 -> 0.35. overall recall@10 now 0.66 -> 0.72.
sam: good sign. that suggests calibration noise + per-tensor issue. add short-query holdout and norm histogram check to onboard checklist.
drew: creating PR with per-channel default for compact models and a short-query holdout: https://git.redwood/tanager/PR-410. pinging for review.
talia: also try optional whitening preproc in eval harness (mean-center + unit-variance) to see if centroids stabilize; sometimes mean-shift after quant causes kmeans brittleness.
drew: ran whitening (post-embed) toggle: silhouette +0.03 and short recall +0.02 over per-channel baseline. small help but not necessary if per-channel fixes most.
ops-bot: action items logged: [add short-query holdout to onboard checklist, enable per-channel by default for compact ptq, add k-sensitivity sweep step, add norm hist diagnostic]. ticket: MEL-824.
drew: plan: merge PR, run dedicated-staging per-channel job for 24h synthetic load to catch tail cases, then promote int8 if stable. will post eval-bot output when complete. thanks for quick triage. :thumbsup:
